scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is AITA (Ask if it's a thing, AITA) or not. Let me break down the situation step by step. First, the person is in a relationship with someone who works full-time from 7am to 7pm. She has a weekend job from 9am to 12pm. They don't live together but are local, so they're often at each other's homes. Her 12-year-old son wants to play football on weekends, which she initially thought to ask her boyfriend to pay for. However, her mom told her it's her responsibility, so she ended up paying by extending her work hours to 9-5. She then asked her boyfriend to pick up and drop off her son on weekends because she's at work. He was uncomfortable and suggested his dad do it, but the dad lives in South London, while they're in North London, and the dad doesn't drive. The boyfriend does drive, so the trip would take 15 minutes for him but over an hour for his dad. She snapped at him, questioning if he wanted to be part of the family and if he wouldn't mind doing small things like this. He got angry, saying he's working longer hours to support her and the son, and he wants to use weekends for his own activities like football games since she's not home anyway. He suggested breaking up because she's putting too many responsibilities on him. She was upset, thinking it's over a football game, and her mom called her, telling her she's out of line. So, is she AITA? Let's consider the dynamics here. She's a single parent with a full-time job and a weekend job. Her boyfriend is also working full-time. She's trying to manage her son's activities, which is a big responsibility. She asked her boyfriend for help, which is reasonable, but he's already stretched thin with his work. He's trying to have some downtime on weekends, which is understandable. She snapped at him, which might have made the situation worse. She questioned his commitment, which could have made him feel defensive. He's already contributing by working longer hours, so asking him to take on more might feel like too much. Her mom's reaction also adds pressure, making her feel like she's overstepping. On the other hand, she's trying to balance her responsibilities, and it's tough. She might feel that her boyfriend should be more involved since he's been in her life for three years. But he's also juggling his own work and personal time. I think the key points are: she's asking for help, but the timing and the way she asked might have been the issue. She snapped, which can escalate conflicts. He's already working long hours and wants his weekends free. She's feeling the burden of her responsibilities and maybe expects more support, but he might feel he's already giving enough. So, is she AITA? It's a bit of both. She has valid reasons for asking, but the way she approached it and the timing might have been off. She might have come on too strong, making him feel overwhelmed. It's a tough spot for both of them, but she could have handled the communication more gently.
